criteria.criterion: A test stops a job at the planning cap with a fixture critic. `athena retry` of it gives the planner the kept round-3 plan and the critic's findings. The first critic round of the retry sees the revised plan, and the retry does only one revision round before the critic. Run: cargo test --locked (named test).
criteria.evidence: I ran `a_retry_of_a_job_stopped_at_the_planning_cap_resumes_from_the_kept_plan` and it passed. In the test, the critic answers revise three times and the job fails with PLANNING_CAP_REASON. The retry's first planner prompt contains the kept round-3 approach and both round-3 findings, and none of the round-1 or round-2 text. After the mark, the calls run exactly Planner, Critic, Producer. The first critic prompt of the retry contains REVISED and not KEPT. The retry has no job-plan-2, and its job-plan-1 has resumed_from set to the old job. In run.rs, plan_round now takes the seed as its initial `revision`, so round 1 of the retry is the revision.

criteria.criterion: A test shows a retry of a job that stopped for any other reason (e.g. timeout, verification failure) still starts the planner with a fresh plan and receives no kept plan. Run: cargo test --locked.
criteria.evidence: I ran `a_retry_of_a_job_that_stopped_for_any_other_reason_plans_fresh` and it passed. It covers three stops: a critic reject, a producer timeout and a failed verification. In each case the retry's planner prompt has no '## Revision' section, no kept approach and no findings, and resumed_from is None. A reading.rs unit test also passed: it shows there is no seed after a reject, a misread reading, a planner failure, a timeout, a verification failure, a non-retry request, or a kept critique that is not 'revise'.

criteria.criterion: athena status prints planning rounds and planning cost per landed job, computed from job records. A test with fixture records asserts the printed numbers, including a before/after split. Run: cargo test --locked.
criteria.evidence: status.rs adds planning_cost(&Records). It follows each landed job's retry chain, counts job-plan records and sums planner and critic invocation cost, and splits landed jobs at the dispatch of the first job with a resumed plan. StatusView.planning_cost is filled from records, and display::status prints it. Four status tests with hand-built Records passed; they assert chain and own means for both groups, the cutover job id and time, the exclusions, and a chain cycle guard. A display test passed that asserts the printed lines, e.g. 'before: 4 landed · 5.5 rounds, $1.25 per job (own 3.0, $0.75)'. The printed-text test starts from a hand-built PlanningCost rather than records, but together the two tests cover records to numbers to text.

criteria.criterion: The kept plan and findings are stored with the job as records, with no secrets or personal data.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: the kept plan and findings are the stopped job's existing job-plan-<n>.json and critique-<n>.json records, which planning_resume_seed reads. The only new data is the optional `resumed_from: Option<JobId>` on JobPlan. It is skipped when None, and old records still parse; I ran the records.rs round-trip test and it passed. The fixtures contain no secrets or personal data. The lifecycle test asserts that check_history reports no violations.

criteria.criterion: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked all exit 0.
criteria.evidence: From Athena's recorded checks on this tree: fmt passed, clippy -D warnings passed, and cargo test --locked passed (1346 tests).

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing resumable planning stops and the new status measure.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: Unreleased/Added has two new entries. One covers the resumable planning stop (kept round-3 plan and critique, one revision round then the critic, resumed_from, other stops plan fresh). The other covers the status measure (rounds and cost per landed job, chain totals, 'after' meaning since the first resumed planning).

findings.summary: Two changed files are not on the expected deliverables list: store.rs and admission.rs.
findings.evidence: Each file gets only a one-line `resumed_from: None` added to a test fixture, which the new JobPlan field requires for the code to compile. Both files were on the planned files list. This adds no behavior.

findings.summary: The status output test renders a hand-built PlanningCost instead of printing from fixture records end to end.
findings.evidence: The record-to-number path is tested in status.rs and the number-to-text path in display.rs, but no single test runs `athena status` over fixture records and checks the printed numbers.

findings.summary: A resumed retry still gets the full round cap, so 'one revision round, then the critic' holds only for the first round.
findings.evidence: The seed only replaces the initial revision. If the critic answers 'revise' again, the retry runs up to max_rounds more. This matches the request and leaves the cap unchanged, which the brief puts out of scope.

summary: Verdict: pass. When a job stops at the planning round cap with a 'revise' verdict, it now keeps its round-3 job-plan and critique records. `athena retry` of that job starts the planner from them: one revision round, then the critic reviews the revised plan. Retries of jobs that stopped for any other reason (a reject, a timeout, a failed verification) still plan fresh. `athena status` adds planning rounds and planning cost per landed job, computed from records. It counts the whole retry chain behind each landed job, with the landed job's own figures beside it, and splits before/after at the first resumed planning. I ran the named lifecycle tests, the reading, status, display and records unit tests, and all passed. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. The CHANGELOG describes both changes. Findings, all minor or smaller: store.rs and admission.rs changed outside the expected deliverables list, but each only gets a one-line test fixture fix the new field requires; the printed-status test renders a hand-built PlanningCost rather than going end to end from records; and a nit that a resumed retry can still use the full round cap if the critic asks for revisions again.
